newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica line use to offset market loss.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica line use to offset market loss.

text.p: Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica will offset any loss in market share due to liberalisation with the increased use of its telephone lines and growth in demand for services, its chairman said on Thursday.

"We're going to lose market share but we expect to compensate for this loss with the elasticity of demand, with a growth of the market and with a bigger use of the networks," Juan Villalonga told a parliamentary committee.

The company aims to increase the use of its lines in the domestic market from 9.9 minutes/day to 13.6 in the year 2000. At the same time, Villalonga hopes to increase penetration from 40 lines per 100 inhabitants to 48 or 52.

In the mobile telephone market, where Telefonica already faces competition and has 80 percent of the market, the company expects the number of clients to climb from 2.8 million to eight million by the end of the decade.

Villalonga also said that the international business of the company would centre on the countries where it already had a presence and where there was great growth potential: Peru, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.
